title: Document structure and metadata
summary: Write a complete HTML document with doctype, language, head metadata, and a body.

scenario.briefing: The storefront page is missing its document shell. Browsers guess the encoding and language, and assistive technology has no title. Build the full HTML document around the existing heading.

objectives.description: Add the doctype, html, head, and body structure.
Provide charset, viewport, and title metadata.

hints: Start with <!doctype html> and wrap everything in html with a lang attribute.
The head carries charset, viewport, and title; the body carries visible content.
Keep the existing h1 inside the body.
Use <!doctype html>, <html lang="en">, <meta charset="utf-8">, <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">, and <title>Campus store</title>.

misconceptions.description: Omitting the doctype and relying on browser quirks mode.
misconceptions.feedback: The doctype tells the browser to use standards mode. Without it, layout and parsing can fall back to legacy quirks.

misconceptions.description: Placing the title element in the body.
misconceptions.feedback: The title belongs in the head. Browsers use it for the tab and search results, and assistive technology announces it before the page content.

sections.title: A document has a shell
sections.body: An HTML document begins with a doctype, then an html element with a lang attribute. The head holds metadata such as charset, viewport, and title. The body holds the visible content.

sections.title: Metadata is not decoration
sections.body: The charset declaration prevents mojibake, the viewport rule keeps mobile layouts readable, and the title names the page for tabs, search results, and screen readers.

vocabulary.definition: The declaration that puts the browser in standards mode.
The container for metadata about the document.
The visible area of the page on a device.

steps.title: Document and metadata claims
hints: The title names the page for tabs and search.
Reject placing the title in the body.

statements.label: Charset, viewport, and title belong in the head.
The title element can live in the body without consequence.
The viewport meta keeps mobile browsers from scaling the page unpredictably.
The lang attribute on html helps screen readers choose pronunciation.

steps.explanation: Metadata lives in the head and describes the document. The body holds visible content.
